newsitem.title: USA: CEI sees power back Wed for most Ohio users.
newsitem.headline: CEI sees power back Wed for most Ohio users.

text.p: Cleveland Electric Illuminating Co (CEI) said Tuesday it hoped to restore power to most of its Ohio customers whose service was disrupted a snow storm that swept into the area last weekend.
"We're looking at most (power) restored tomorrow," said CEI spokesman Jim Sielicki.
The ongoing outages were concentrated in areas east of Cleveland, he said.
"We've got 20,000 still without power. Yesterday we had 46,000," Sielicki said, adding a total of 175,000 of CEI's customers experienced service interruption of varying duration since last weekend.
Cleveland itself, so far, received six inches of snow, compared with its southern suburb of Chardon which was dumped with four and a half to five feet.
The weekend snowfall has continued into today.
"It makes it difficult for repairs," he said, noting new outages spurred by additional precipitation.
Most main electricity feeder lines were restored to operation, with only four out today compared with 32 at the height of the outage, Sielicki said.
He said 350 repair crews, including 50 from neighboring electric companies, continued to clear fallen trees and downed power lines.
Cleveland Electric Illuminating is a subsidiary of Centerior Energy Corp.
